hints.content: To translate quadrilateral $ABCD$ by $1$ unit to the right and $4$ units up, we basically translate quadrilateral $ABCD$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{B(-4,3)}$ is translated to $\greenD{(-3,7)}$.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at negative two, negative five, B at negative four, three, C at six, two, and D at six, negative two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves one unit right from vertex B and up.four units to a point at negative three, seven.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at negative two, negative five, B at negative four, three, C at six, two, and D at six, negative two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves one unit right from the four vertices and up.four units to form an inage of a congruent quadrilateral with vertices at negative one, negative one, negative three, seven, seven, six, and seven, two.

question.content:
